title: preview-check failure diagnostics are garbled by fmt brace-collision — a red run cannot show which edge set diverged
evidence: fmt.aprintf("S1: preview edges %v, want {0-1,1-2}", prev.edges) — the literal braces are parsed as fmt directives ("{0" = argument-index verb), so on failure the message renders as "want %!(MISSING CLOSE BRACE)1,1-2}". Reproduced live: mutating the preview's DAG edges in a worktree copy produced "FAIL S1: preview edges [...], want %!(MISSING CLOSE BRACE)1,1-2}" and "FAIL S6: ... want %!(BAD ARGUMENT NUMBER)%!(MISSING CLOSE BRACE)3,3-4}". Four sites affected: S1 edges (L237), S2 edges (L283), S3 split nodes (L335), S6 edges (L429).
detail: The green path is unaffected (7/7 scenarios pass; verified locally). But this gate exists precisely for the moment a regression lands — and at that moment the printed diagnosis, the only human-readable signal of WHAT diverged, is unreadable garbage. This degrades the acceptance criterion's operational value ("every scenario's preview DAG edge set + cost match the sim's rebuilt routing table") even though the comparison itself is sound and non-vacuous (verified: cost-accumulation corruption -> 4 reds; DAG-edge corruption -> 4 reds).
recommended_fix: Escape the braces ({{0-1,1-2}} per Odin fmt rules) or drop them from the prose ("want edges 0-1 and 1-2") in all four fmt.aprintf failure strings; build a fixture string for the want-set instead of inlining brace delimiters in the format text.

title: Assist config in data/assist.json (not balance.json) — deviation from the briefing's "N in balance.json" is correctly flagged and its rationale verified sound
evidence: Verified the claimed poison: core/catalog.odin:794 catalogs_hash_sources folds src.balance (every byte of balance.json) into catalog_hash, which binds the T1 replay header (determinism_test.odin:283 pins header.catalog_hash == cat.hash) — so ANY field addition to balance.json re-blesses all 16 blessed goldens, a direct hit on the spec's STRICT golden clause (acceptance 5). The cited precedent exists: core/topology.odin:306 PLACEMENT_MIN_SEP_TILES carries the same "not in balance.json because golden-poisoned" comment. assist.json follows the palette.json cosmetic-class pattern (core/catalog.odin:781: palette is deliberately NOT hashed). Config load is ODN-5-clean: assist_config_load falls back to inline defaults on any parse error (malformed config cannot brick the run); graduation_n/glow_ticks/nudge_ticks are range-validated. The spec's "Ask First: nothing expected — the acceptance hierarchy resolves the balance.json conflict (STRICT golden clause wins)" is the right call and the deviation is flagged for the human in both the frozen spec and the PR body.
detail: Acceptance lens verdict: the deviation does not violate any acceptance criterion — the briefing's "N in balance.json" was a data-driven-ODN-5 suggestion, and the STRICT golden-identity acceptance criterion is the higher law; the minion resolved the conflict per the hierarchy, documented it, and flagged the human. No fix required in this round; the deferred move-back-to-balance.json at the next legitimate re-bless is already planned.
recommended_fix: None for this PR. Keep the deviation flag visible for the human (already done in spec + PR body); optionally add the planned "move this block to balance.json at the next legitimate re-bless" note to the canon/GDD docs when that re-bless lands.

title: Per-edge Dag_Edge.cost fields are computed twice but never cross-checked nor rendered — only the path total is pinned
evidence: The cross-check's edges_match compares only the normalized (u,v) node-pair sets; the per-edge cost fields (Dag_Edge.cost, filled by min_bundle_cost in the preview and check_min_cost in the sim walk) are never compared against each other, and the renderer (draw_glow_edge, app/render/assist.odin:410-448) never reads them. Empirically confirmed: a mutation that added +1 to every appended Dag_Edge.cost left preview-check 7/7 green (only a mutation of the dist accumulation — the total — produced reds).
detail: What the player sees (the ONE 'route N' number) IS fully pinned: prev.cost is compared against the sim-walk total in all positive scenarios, and the total equals the table's dist at dst by the ECMP invariant. So there is no user-facing correctness gap today. The risk is latent: a future per-edge pricing divergence (e.g. someone changes min_bundle_cost to price a mixed-tier bundle differently) would be invisible to the gate as long as it preserves the total, and the edge cost fields would silently lie. They are currently dead weight — computed in two mirrors and consumed by neither the check nor the render.
recommended_fix: Either (a) extend edges_match to also verify each edge's cost field against the expected per-edge cost (cheap, makes the mirrors real), or (b) drop the cost field from Dag_Edge entirely and let the total carry the only cost signal. Option (a) is preferable — it closes the triplication drift risk the architecture/codebase lenses also flagged.
